vulnerabilities.title: WordPress Config Backup Exposed
vulnerabilities.description: A backup of wp-config.php containing database credentials may be accessible.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Remove backup files from the web root.

vulnerabilities.title: Missing Content Security Policy (CSP)
vulnerabilities.description: No Content-Security-Policy header found. This makes the application vulnerable to XSS and data injection attacks.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Implement a strict CSP. Start with: Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; object-src 'none'

vulnerabilities.title: Git Repository Exposed
vulnerabilities.description: Git repository configuration is exposed.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Remove .git directory or block access via web server configuration.

vulnerabilities.title: WordPress Debug Log Exposed
vulnerabilities.description: WordPress debug log may contain sensitive information.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Disable WP_DEBUG_LOG in production or move logs outside web root.

vulnerabilities.title: Backup/Sensitive Files Exposed (26 found)
vulnerabilities.description: Backup or sensitive configuration files are publicly accessible.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Remove backup files from web root or restrict access.
vulnerabilities.evidence: Files found: web.config, web.config.bak, web.config.old, .htaccess, .htaccess.bak, .htpasswd, config.php, config.php.bak, config.inc.php, database.yml

vulnerabilities.title: Missing X-Frame-Options Header
vulnerabilities.description: X-Frame-Options header is missing. The site may be vulnerable to clickjacking attacks.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Add 'X-Frame-Options: DENY' or 'X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN' header.

vulnerabilities.title: Missing X-Content-Type-Options Header
vulnerabilities.description: X-Content-Type-Options header is missing. Browsers may MIME-sniff responses, potentially executing malicious content.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Add 'X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff' header.

vulnerabilities.title: Missing Referrer-Policy Header
vulnerabilities.description: Referrer-Policy header is missing. Sensitive information may leak via the Referer header.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Add 'Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin' or 'no-referrer' header.

vulnerabilities.title: Missing Permissions-Policy Header
vulnerabilities.description: Permissions-Policy (formerly Feature-Policy) header is missing. Browser features are not restricted.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Add Permissions-Policy header to restrict features: Permissions-Policy: geolocation=(), camera=(), microphone=()

vulnerabilities.title: Forms Missing CSRF Protection
vulnerabilities.description: Found 1 form(s) without visible CSRF token protection.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Implement CSRF tokens in all state-changing forms.

vulnerabilities.title: Potential HTTP Request Smuggling Vector
vulnerabilities.description: The server accepts requests with conflicting Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding headers, which may indicate vulnerability to HTTP request smuggling.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Configure the server to reject requests with conflicting Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding headers. Ensure proper HTTP parsing at all layers.
vulnerabilities.evidence: Server accepted request with both Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding headers. Response status: 200

vulnerabilities.title: WordPress User Enumeration via REST API
vulnerabilities.description: User enumeration is possible through the WordPress REST API.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Disable user enumeration by restricting access to /wp-json/wp/v2/users endpoint.

vulnerabilities.title: WordPress Uploads Directory Listing
vulnerabilities.description: Directory listing is enabled on uploads folder.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Disable directory listing or add index file.

vulnerabilities.title: Server Version Disclosure
vulnerabilities.description: The Server header reveals web server software and version information.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Remove or obfuscate the Server header to hide implementation details.

vulnerabilities.title: ASP.NET Version Disclosure
vulnerabilities.description: X-AspNet-Version header reveals the ASP.NET version.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Remove X-AspNet-Version header via web.config or IIS configuration.

vulnerabilities.title: WordPress XML-RPC Enabled
vulnerabilities.description: XML-RPC is enabled which can be used for brute-force attacks.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Disable XML-RPC if not needed or use a plugin to restrict access.

vulnerabilities.title: WordPress Version Exposed
vulnerabilities.description: WordPress readme.html reveals version information.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Remove or restrict access to readme.html.

vulnerabilities.title: WordPress Includes Directory Accessible
vulnerabilities.description: WordPress includes directory is accessible.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Restrict access to wp-includes directory.

vulnerabilities.title: Robots.txt Found
vulnerabilities.description: Sensitive path '/robots.txt' is accessible (HTTP 200).
vulnerabilities.remediation: Restrict access to this path or remove it from production.

vulnerabilities.title: API Endpoints Discovered (38 found)
vulnerabilities.description: Discovered 38 API endpoints.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Ensure all API endpoints have proper authentication and authorization.

vulnerabilities.title: Hidden Parameters Discovered (98 found)
vulnerabilities.description: Discovered 98 potentially active parameters.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Test discovered parameters for injection vulnerabilities.
vulnerabilities.evidence: Parameters: from, page, tpl, api_key, authorization, filepath, cb, username, dir, doc

vulnerabilities.title: WordPress REST API Accessible
vulnerabilities.description: WordPress REST API is accessible.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Review REST API endpoints for sensitive data exposure.
